leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2012 Human Rights Report - Central African Republic
leads.documents: Penal Code criminalization of 'public expression of love' between persons of same sex, penalties of 6 months to 2 years or 150,000-600,000 CFA francs, enhanced penalties when child involved, and that there were no reports police arrested or detained persons under these provisions in 2012; also societal discrimination entrenched and attributed to Western influence.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "U.S. Department of State's 2012 human rights report" and "U.S. Department of State's 2012 Human Rights Report"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2023 Human Rights Report - Central African Republic
leads.documents: Living conditions in 2023: religious preaching conversion rarely enacted because LGBTQ identities kept hidden, concealment due to criminalization and stigma, unclear whether lack of reported violence reflects lack of incidents or non-reporting, discrimination in education, healthcare and employment.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "The 2023 Human Rights Report"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Constitution of the Central African Republic, Article 7
leads.documents: Constitutional ban on same-sex marriage; marriage defined as 'the union between one man and one woman ... Family and marriage are under the protection of the State'; no legal recognition of same-sex couples.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "Article 7 of the Constitution"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Central African Republic Penal Code - public expression of love provision
leads.documents: Legal status of same-sex sexual activity as legal but criminalization of public displays/expression of love between same-sex persons with fines and imprisonment.
leads.detail: Cited via U.S. Department of State 2012 report summary in text; no separate URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Law 24-001 on the Protection of Personal Data, Article 17
leads.documents: Protects sexual orientation as sensitive data; Article 17 states 'Any processing of sensitive data is prohibited due to risks of discrimination or infringement of personal freedoms.'
leads.detail: Cited in text as "Law 24-001 on the Protection of Personal Data" Article 17; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: French government website on adoption
leads.documents: Adoption eligibility in Central African Republic - single and married people eligible to adopt; does not state whether single LGBTQ people are disqualified.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "a website of the French government"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Alternatives Centrafrique - Universal Periodic Review third cycle submission
leads.documents: Local LGBTQ organization submissions to UPR documenting LGBTQ situation in Central African Republic.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "submitted reports for the Universal Periodic Review's third and fourth cycle"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Alternatives Centrafrique - Universal Periodic Review fourth cycle report
leads.documents: Organization founded 2009 and registered 2020; documented cases of arrests due to false accusations of same-sex intercourse; mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "According to its fourth cycle report"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Central African Republic National HIV Plan 2016 to 2020 - Global Fund Project
leads.documents: Recognized men who have sex with men as a key population for the Global Fund Project to focus on; context of HIV stigma leading to workplace harassment, blackmail and firings.
leads.detail: Cited in text as "country's National HIV Plan from 2016 to 2020"; no URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: United Nations joint statement on ending acts of violence and related human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.documents: Central African Republic as one of few African states signing joint statement condemning violence and discrimination against LGBTQ people.
leads.detail: Cited in text as '"joint statement on ending acts of violence and related human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity" at the United Nations'; no URL visible in provided text.
